_howToEdit: THIS IS THE ONLY FILE YOU NEED TO EDIT TO CHANGE YOUR TEXT, PROJECTS AND LINKS.
1. Change only the words between the quotation marks. Keep every quote mark, comma, bracket and brace exactly where it is.
2. Wrap a word in *single stars* to make it stand out (red italic-style), or **double stars** for bold. Example: "I build *systems*".
3. To ADD a project: copy one whole { ... } block inside "projects", paste it right after another block, put a comma between the two blocks, then edit the words.
4. To HIDE something without deleting it, add "draft": true to that block. Drafts show up (with a red tag) on your own computer when you run `npm run dev`, but never on the live site.

5. Photos: the hero portrait is src/assets/portrait/1-front.webp (a square 1280x1280 picture on a black background; extra files in that folder become a scroll turn), and the small photo on the profile card is src/assets/card/id.webp (4:5, 400x500). Replace them keeping the names (README.md explains how they are made). Résumé and CV: replace public/Taanshu-Babariya-Resume.pdf and public/Taanshu-Babariya-CV.pdf with the new files, keeping the same names.
6. When you are done: git add . then git commit -m "update" then git push. Netlify republishes the site in about a minute.
7. "site" → "url" must be the real web address of the site. Change it only if the address changes (for example a custom domain); README.md lists the two other places to update.
If the site stops building after an edit, it is almost always a missing comma or quote. Paste this file into jsonlint.com and it will point at the exact line.

about.lead: I’m Taanshu, an AI/ML engineering student in Mumbai who turns models into working products.
paragraphs: I’m studying Artificial Intelligence & Machine Learning at St. Francis Institute of Technology. My recent work centres on graph neural networks for financial fraud detection: I took a hackathon prototype all the way to a measured, leakage-free deep-learning study. Alongside it I completed the Krutanic AI/ML training program, built a voice-driven personal AI assistant, and delivered websites for real businesses as a freelance developer.

Most real problems are signal buried in noise — a fraud ring inside a million transactions, a strong candidate behind a weak headline, a real advance inside forty pages of “state of the art”. I like building systems that find it, and can say how they found it.
principles: Find the signal before choosing the model.
A model should explain what it caught, and own what it missed.
Ship it so someone else can break it.

projects.title: FraudScope
projects.subtitle: Temporal graph learning for financial-fraud detection.
description: Born as **FundTrace AI**, a real-time anti-money-laundering platform built for Hackathon Round 2 (PS3: Banking Fraud Detection) at K. J. Somaiya College of Engineering. An edge-aware GraphSAGE classifier, fused with a rule engine and Isolation Forest, flags layering, round-tripping, structuring and mule accounts as transactions stream in. On held-out synthetic data it reached F1 0.944 and PR-AUC 0.980, against F1 0.080 for rules alone.
Then extended into a leakage-free deep-learning study: a temporal GNN against GraphSAGE and Random Forest, on a strict past-to-future split.
projects.note: 97,831 transactions · 5,000 accounts · past-to-future split · mean of 3 seeds
